operations.new: 8.1 Suppose $S=1$. Then $D=1$ by [F3], every Bellman vector $h_k$ has a single coordinate, and both transition rows are the point mass at the only state. Hence $(Ph_k)(S_t,A_t)-h_k(S_t)=0$ and $(q_k-P)h_k=0$ identically. The episode endpoint differences and the transition martingale increments $X_t$ in step 4.1 are also zero. Therefore re-summing the pointwise inequality in step 3.1, and retaining the reward martingale bound from step 4.1, gives on that same joint event $$\Delta_T\le[\sqrt{14L_r}+1]Q_T+\sqrt{\frac T2\log(4/\delta)}.$$ Here $2b^r_k(s,a)\le\sqrt{14L_r}/\sqrt{\max\{1,N_k(s,a)\}}$, while $\varepsilon_k=1/\sqrt{t_k}\le1/\sqrt{\max\{1,N_k(s,a)\}}$. Thus both the nonzero reward-confidence sum and the reward martingale remain present. If $A\le T$, then $L_r\le3L$ and $\log(4/\delta)\le2L$. Dividing the displayed inequality by $B=\sqrt{ATL}$ and using step 5.1 yields $$\frac{\Delta_T}{B}\le(1+\sqrt2)\left(\sqrt{\frac{14L_r}{L}}+\frac1{\sqrt L}\right)+\sqrt{\frac{\log(4/\delta)}{2AL}}\le(1+\sqrt2)\left(\sqrt{42}+\frac1{\sqrt L}\right)+1<\frac52\left(\frac{13}2+\frac32\right)+1=21<34.$$ The last strict inequality uses $L\ge\log2>1/2$, $\sqrt2<3/2$, and $\sqrt{42}<13/2$. The case $A>T$ was already covered in step 7.1. This completes the first assertion for every fixed $T\ge2$. Enlarging its logarithm gives the second assertion for those horizons. At $T=1$, $\Delta_1\le1$, whereas $34DS\sqrt{A\log(2/\delta)}>1$, proving the second assertion at the remaining boundary with probability one. [given, F1, F3, step 3.1, step 4.1, step 5.1, step 6.1, step 7.1, algebra] ∎
